name: C2a1a3 (F1918)
description: C2a1a3 (F1918) is a subclade of C2a1a distributed across East Asia, found in Chinese, Korean, and Southeast Asian populations. It is characterized by the F1918 SNP marker and represents a distinct lineage that diverged during the early Neolithic demographic expansion of East Asia. C2a1a3 has a somewhat broader geographic range than its sister clades, extending into parts of Southeast Asia through ancient population movements associated with the spread of rice agriculture.
interestingFact: The F1918 marker defines a branch of haplogroup C that accompanied the early spread of East Asian agricultural populations southward into Southeast Asia, providing a genetic signal of ancient continental East Asian migration routes predating historical records.
references: Wei et al. (2018) — Phylogenetic analysis of the Y-chromosome haplogroup C2b-F1067. PLOS ONE 13(5), e0197744.
